answer.evidence: The chair is an L-shaped blue silhouette: a narrow backrest at rows 0-2 and a 16px-wide body at rows 3-10. The light rows at 4 and 8 (L=157) are the same color as the top and bottom of the outline, so they read as a bevel border around a flat blue panel, not a front-edge line of a seat top. The only dark underside is rows 9-10 (2 rows), too thin to count as a front face. No seat ellipse or visible seat surface is drawn. Rows 11-15 are gray floor tiles with pale posts, not part of the chair's top. Overall this is a side profile of a toppled chair with no seat seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small single-tile prop, a toppled blue chair, so I judged it mostly by eye next to prop-bench-wood and prop-hedge. It has 9 distinct colours and a median of 9 per tile, close to the hedge (10 per tile, 11 colours) and near the bench (14 colours). It is below the richer stall and well, which are much larger pieces. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no 5x5 blocks of one colour. Only 11% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline leans dark blue rather than black. That fits the Beodeul habit of tinting the outline to the adjacent material. The blue ramp has about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark/outline), against roughly 5 on the references. Texture is modest, with small value breaks on the seat and back, but at this size it would not look thinner or more sticker-like beside the bench. Slightly lower in density than the best references, but acceptable.
